answer: Stop sybils with a river, a kernel, and a sparrow. Each epoch a kernel salts one river per identity: a one-way chain of checkpoints crossed in order, each stamp carried by a sparrow courier who can bear only one stamp per epoch. The river toll doubles at each checkpoint, so a full crossing costs far more than one toll. A kernel that salts a second river for the same funder loses its whole bond, and every stamp on the cloned river is voided with it. One honest agent pays for one river crossing; N clones pay for N river crossings at doubling tolls and need N sparrow couriers, for one share.
